dek: A Baltimore pick seller that says it started with the 1992 football season. Its Lock Club costs $500 a week, $1500 a month or $5000 a season per sport, and a cheaper Financial Program runs $75 to $599. Sales run through advisors on the phone, the terms say all services are non refundable unless a receipt says otherwise, and every record we saw is a run chosen by the seller.

short_answer: ATS Consultants is a real, long running pick seller. Its current site, atsbas.com, gives a Baltimore street address, a toll free number, an international number, a fax number, written terms under Maryland law, and published prices. Press releases from 2009 and 2012 and a 2014 interview show the same firm, the same 800 number and the same founders' names. In that narrow sense the business is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money is a separate question that nothing we opened answers. The Proven Results page is a long list of hot runs and highlighted weekends, such as "WON 20 out of 24 weeks last season" and "Football Lock Club has now won 9 of the last 12 weeks", chosen by the seller. The newest block on that page lists 16 different picks and every one is marked WON. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick with odds.

The few independent words about ATS are old and mostly negative: a 2011 Sportsbook Review thread where a member said a friend kept losing with the firm, and a 2014 post in the same thread claiming ATS and another service sent out the same five plays. In 2012 the firm also publicly apologized for promoting wins with ticket images that it later said showed projections, not real payouts. Treat ATS as an expensive seller with marketing records, not a proven winner.
pricing_intro: Both tables were on the atsbas.com Lock Club page on 20 Nov 2026, unchanged from our 16 Nov check. The page says "Combination programs and ALL SPORT services are available" without prices. We saw no checkout; the page points buyers to "Speak With an Advisor". The Financial Program page itself shows no prices and also sends buyers to an advisor.

guarantee: The Lock Club page makes no guarantee. The Financial Program page says it is "Backed by a full money-back guarantee" and ends with "Join today with a Money-back Guarantee!", but we found no written rules for that guarantee on the page: no grading period, no unit count, no claim process.

The site terms are strict. They say "Please note that all ATS Services are non-refundable unless explicitly specified otherwise on receipt." Once a package is bought and its first pick is released, "the package is non-cancellable under any circumstances." And "A “Money Back Guarantee” is valid only for certain packages or programs where it is explicitly mentioned in writing."

The terms also say "no assurance can be given of winning or profiting from our selections", and any dispute goes to state or federal court in Baltimore under Maryland law. The weekly review PDF carries a similar line: "Performance figures and projections supplied by ATS; future results are not guaranteed." A buyer should get any guarantee written on the receipt before paying. Betting losses are never covered.

claims_note: How we checked: we read the whole Proven Results page on 20 Nov 2026 and counted every pick it lists with a result. The 2024 football table shows 45 picks over five weekends, 37 won and 8 lost, which is 82% winners. The two 2025 football example weeks show 17 picks, 12 won and 5 lost. The newest 2026 block lists 18 entries, but two picks appear twice, leaving 16 different picks, all marked WON. A long middle section from late 2024 to early 2025 lists about 176 picks across all sports, 130 won and 46 lost by our count. Every block was chosen by the seller, and the page never shows a full week by week list.

The experience claim shifts from page to page: 34 years on the About headline and the Lock Club page, 33 years in the About stat block, and "Celebrating Thirty Years" on the homepage. One 2024 headline says "+20 Units Sept 14th" while the table beneath it lists that weekend as 20 Sept. Small, but the copy is not kept consistent.

The win rate claims have moved a lot over time. In 2009 the firm claimed over 66% for a football season, in 2014 a staff member said clients were on the right side 90% of the time, and the 2026 site talks in weekly runs and units without any overall rate. "Units" are never defined, most football picks show a spread with no price, and the dollar figures assume a $250 unit.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every ATS pick with the line, the odds and the release time, and no third party tracking of the service.

What the seller publishes: the Proven Results page lists weekly highlights by sport, some with teams, lines and scores, and the homepage links a weekly review PDF. The issue we read, Vol. 13 for 18 to 23 Nov 2026, runs 27 pages of power ratings, previews and trends, plus headlines such as "HOCKEY LOCK CLUB WINS 6 OF 7 WEEKS" and "FOOTBALL PROJECTED TO WIN From now through the Super Bowl". These are selected examples and forecasts, not a record. Tags such as "(ffp)" and "(el)" are not explained.

One public record about the firm's marketing does exist. On 30 Jun 2012 ATS put out a release with images of winning tickets, tied to a large preseason bet on the Miami Heat and other wagers. On 2 Jul 2012 it apologized. The company president, Jordan Runco, said the amounts shown were a projection of what clients won based on the firm's forecasts, that the firm never intended to cash the tickets, that it had no relationship with the casinos and track named, and "We overstepped on this, and take full responsibility for it."

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no ATS Consultants pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how ATS Consultants performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the 2009 release claimed over 66% winners, a 2014 interview claimed 90%, and the 2024 weekends ATS chose to show come to 82%. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard odds of 110 to win 100 a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on ATS Consultants is thin and old. Almost everything online about the firm was written by the firm. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found one independent discussion of ATS Consultants: an 18 post Sportsbook Review thread from 2011 and 2014. Five posts there talk about ATS directly. One member said a friend had lost with ATS several times, another said the firm's marketing pointed to a perfect record on its Wednesday football plays, and a 2014 post claimed ATS and another service sent out the same five college basketball plays at the same line. One post was mildly positive at second hand: an acquaintance had paid ATS for years and said it made money if you could live through the cold streaks. None of these posters said they had bought from ATS themselves. Everything else is the firm's own material: 2009 press releases and free pick posts that end with a phone number to enroll, a 2014 interview, the 2012 apology for misleading ticket images, and the current atsbas.com results page. We found no Reddit post from 2024 on, no Covers thread, no BBB file and no court or regulator action. That is too little for a pattern, but the little there is leans negative.

The member who opened a Sportsbook Review thread asking whether anyone had paid ATS for picks said a friend had been burned by the firm about three times and could not explain why they kept paying for picks that kept losing. Another member in the same thread questioned how the firm had stayed in business so long, and a third pointed to its advertised perfect record on Wednesday football plays as marketing. None posted a record.

In the same thread a member said someone they knew had paid ATS for years and claimed it was profitable as long as you could endure the cold streaks, with strong results on horse racing. The member stressed they had never used ATS themselves and was not endorsing it.

A member wrote that ATS and another pick service had released the same five college basketball plays at the same line, said they did not think the other service was copying ATS, and called ATS one of the worst operators in the business. We could not check the picks they described.

The atsbas.com Proven Results page says ATS has won nearly 40 weeks over the last two years, that the Football Lock Club won 9 of the last 12 weeks, and that average clients have won nearly $50,000 per season over the last five years. These are the seller's own selected results, not buyer reports.

Free ATS picks were republished on Bleacher Report in 2009 under a Touthouse byline. Each post gave one or two free plays and closed with a call to an ATS account executive at 1 800 772 1287, or a newsletter sign up, to enroll in a full season program. This shows how the firm sold, not how buyers fared.
In TheRX daily service play thread, the moderator's opening post lists ATS Consultants under "Do not post write-ups". No ATS plays or buyer comments appeared in that thread.

A Better Business Bureau search for ATS Consultants in Baltimore returned "No Business Profile matched this search". Our saved copy of 438,260 posts from ten betting subreddits, covering 1 Jan 2024 to 15 Nov 2026, has no post naming the firm, and web searches found no Covers thread and no court or regulator action naming it.

conflicts: ATS sells by phone through account executives and advisors, and neither the Lock Club nor the Financial Program page has a checkout. A sales call is where buyers get pitched bigger packages and combination programs whose prices are not posted, so decide your budget before you call.
The 2012 apology shows the firm once advertised client wins with ticket images that, by its own account, were projections. Weigh the current results page with that history in mind.
The weekly review PDF mixes forecasts with results: "FOOTBALL PROJECTED TO WIN" sits on the same cover as hockey win claims. A projection is not a result.

We saw no sportsbook affiliate banners on the atsbas.com pages we read. The 2014 interview ran on a betting news site, and the 2009 free picks ran under a tout directory byline; both were promotional.
strengths: A named firm with a Baltimore street address, toll free, international and fax numbers, an email and written terms under Maryland law.
Prices for every Lock Club and Financial Program package are published on the site.
The firm has used the same name and 800 number since at least 2009, and the same founders are named in releases from 2009 to 2014.
It publicly owned up to a misleading 2012 promotion instead of letting it stand.
Some blocks on the results page do show losses, such as the 2024 weekends with 8 losses in 45 picks.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a run, weekend or total chosen by the seller, and the newest block shows only winners.
The Lock Club is expensive: $500 for one week or $5000 for one season of one sport.
The terms make services non refundable unless the receipt says otherwise and packages non cancellable, while the Financial Program page advertises a full money back guarantee with no written rules.
Dollar claims such as "$250/unit players win $5000" need much bigger bets than one unit per play, and the page never shows the bet sizes.
Win rate claims have ranged from over 66% in 2009 to 90% in 2014, far above what verified long run bettors achieve.
The only independent posts we found are negative or second hand, and a 2014 post alleged the same plays were sold by another service.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds, the bet size and the time it was sent. A list of hot weekends is not a record.
Ask how many units each play is worth. Dollar totals at "$250/unit" mean little if some plays are five or ten units.
Get any money back guarantee written on the receipt. These terms only honor one that is explicit in writing.
Decide your budget before the advisor call, and ask for the price of any combination or all sport program in writing.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real firm with a Baltimore address, phone numbers, written terms and published prices, active under the same name since at least 2009 and, by its own account, since 1992. We could not verify that its picks win over time, because it publishes no full record, and the few independent forum posts we found are old and lean negative.
How much does ATS Consultants cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 the Lock Club cost $500 a week, $1500 a month or $5000 a full season per sport, and the Financial Program cost $75 a week, $199 a month or $599 a season per sport. Combination and all sport programs are sold by phone with no posted price.

The terms say services are non refundable unless the receipt explicitly says otherwise, and packages cannot be cancelled once the first pick is released. The Financial Program page advertises a money back guarantee, so get its terms written on the receipt before paying.
Does ATS Consultants have a verified record?

No. Its Proven Results page shows selected weekends and runs, such as 37 wins and 8 losses over five 2024 football weekends by our count, and claims such as "WON 20 out of 24 weeks last season". No outside service tracks every pick.
What was the 2012 ATS ticket apology about?

In June 2012 ATS promoted big wins, including a preseason Miami Heat title bet, with images of winning tickets. Two days later it said the amounts were a projection of client winnings, that it never meant to cash the tickets, and that it took full responsibility.

For the money you get the plays released in the period you buy, a weekly review newsletter and access to phone advisors. What is unproven is whether the picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at standard odds over hundreds of plays, and at $5000 a season the price alone takes a large bankroll to recover.
